overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of neurophenomenology. You'll be asked about the working hypothesis of mutual constraints, first-person and second-person methods, the design of the Lutz and colleagues readiness study, and criticisms of neurophenomenology.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: What did Varela propose as a remedy for the hard problem?

options.html: A new physical ingredient that explains experience
options.text: A new physical ingredient that explains experience
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Varela rejected the search for an extra ingredient. His remedy was methodological.

options.html: A method joining disciplined reports and neural data
options.text: A method joining disciplined reports and neural data
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! He diagnosed the gap as a lack of method for examining experience.

options.html: A proof that the hard problem is an illusion
options.text: A proof that the hard problem is an illusion
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Varela accepted that the problem was real.

options.html: A theory identifying experience with brain activity
options.text: A theory identifying experience with brain activity
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Varela didn't reduce experience to brain activity. His remedy was methodological.

forms.stemHtml: What distinguishes a second-person method from other first-person methods?

options.html: The participant reports only simple yes-or-no judgments
options.text: The participant reports only simple yes-or-no judgments
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Second-person methods aim at detailed description.

options.html: A trained interviewer guides the person's attention
options.text: A trained interviewer guides the person's attention
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The interviewer guides attention without suggesting content.

options.html: The researcher describes the participant's experience
options.text: The researcher describes the participant's experience
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The participant describes; the interviewer only guides.

options.html: Descriptions are replaced by physiological measures
options.text: Descriptions are replaced by physiological measures
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Second-person methods produce descriptions of experience.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are criticisms raised against neurophenomenology? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Introspection may be unreliable even about current experience
options.text: Introspection may be unreliable even about current experience
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Schwitzgebel argues this about naive introspection.

options.html: Training may shape what participants report
options.text: Training may shape what participants report
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Participants may learn to report what they were trained to notice.

options.html: Results may not scale to large samples or complex tasks
options.text: Results may not scale to large samples or complex tasks
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Studies have been small and labor-intensive.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Neurophenomenology puts first-person experience at its center.

options.html: It averages away all variability between trials
options.text: It averages away all variability between trials
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It aims to recover variability that standard averaging discards.

forms.stemHtml: What is the name of Varela's working hypothesis that first-person descriptions guide the analysis of neural data, and neural findings in turn refine the descriptions? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The constraint runs in both directions.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The answer is "mutual constraints."

forms.stemHtml: In the Lutz and colleagues readiness study, how were participants' reports used?

options.html: To confirm the results after the EEG had been analyzed
options.text: To confirm the results after the EEG had been analyzed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The reports came first and structured the analysis.

options.html: To replace the EEG with self-ratings of attention
options.text: To replace the EEG with self-ratings of attention
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The EEG was analyzed; the reports organized how.

options.html: To sort trials into clusters before EEG analysis
options.text: To sort trials into clusters before EEG analysis
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each cluster was analyzed separately, recovering variability usually averaged away.

options.html: To choose which participants to exclude
options.text: To choose which participants to exclude
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The reports sorted trials into phenomenological clusters.

title: Neurophenomenology
